meta.owner: anti-slop. This corpus is the single labeled corpus for the anti-slop rule set and its downstream distillations. ui-craft's tests/corpus/ is a DOWNSTREAM VIEW of the shared design fixtures, not a second hand-maintained set: fixtures flow anti-slop -> ui-craft, and a fixture edited only in ui-craft is drift, not a change. Per-item ownership for the wider 1.7.0 integration is recorded in docs/rankings-refresh.md, section 'Downstream sync'.
meta.purpose: Ground truth for the precision/recall harness. Each fixture lists the findings a correct scan SHOULD produce, keyed by the scanner's own rule id, plus the severity and confidence the rule carries when it fires.
meta.schema: fixtures[]: { file, modality (prose|code|design|native), role (positive|clean-control|coverage-boundary), expected[], maxIncidentalFindings?, note? }. expected[] entries are { id, severity?, confidence? }: id is the rule key (v.name || v.word || v.phrase || v.type), and severity/confidence record what the rule emits. An entry with no severity/confidence is a KNOWN FALSE NEGATIVE -- the label is correct ground truth and the scanner does not currently reach it.

roles.positive: Plants tells this scanner detects. expected[] is non-empty.
roles.clean-control: Uses the prescribed technique CORRECTLY and must stay silent. A clean control is not 'a file with no tells' -- it is a file that exercises the constructs the doctrine recommends, so it catches the mirror failure: a scanner that has learned to match constructs rather than defects. Two of ui-craft's own controls were latent doctrine violations for several releases, so audit these against current doctrine rather than trusting them.
roles.coverage-boundary: Plants a real tell this scanner has NO rule for. expected[] is empty, but the file is NOT clean and must never be cited as evidence that the tell is absent. These record the scanner's coverage boundary honestly, and guard against a future over-broad rule firing on them by accident.

meta.cleanControlRule: clean-control and coverage-boundary fixtures carry maxIncidentalFindings: the scan may surface at most that many findings before the control is treated as failed. It is 0 on every fixture, because 0 is the policy the suite has always ENFORCED: any finding on a negative fixture is a false positive by construction, and the sibling precision gate in corpus.test.mjs (design tp=49 at 2.1.0, tolerance 0.02) fails on the first one. A declared tolerance of 1 was strictly dominated -- it could never be the failing assertion, so it was dead metadata that read like slack. Enforced by test/corpus-contract.test.mjs.
meta.severityIsInformational: The harness matches on rule id only. severity and confidence are carried so that a change in how a rule GRADES a finding is visible in review and caught by test/corpus-contract.test.mjs, which asserts the labels still match what the scanner emits.

provenance.shared-with-ui-craft: gradient-hero, shadcn-card-kit, frosted-nav-neon, legacy-marketing-page, small-avatar-clean originated here and were copied downstream. presence-single, cream-serif-sage, token-drift, missing-states, clean-intentional, uncommitted-radius, fluid-adaptive-clean, fixed-desktop-shell, viewport-query-card, vh-bottom-bar were authored in ui-craft during its 0.2.4 and 0.3.0 releases and were imported here in anti-slop 1.7.0, at which point this corpus became the single owner of all of them.
provenance.authored-here-in-2.1.0: marketing-defaults, motion-rhythm, gallery-unlabelled, legacy-theme.css, tokens-clean.css, hatched-wordmark, near-miss-controls (design); render-user-card.tsx, ingest_records.py, pasted-snippet.js, hatched-onboarding.js, order-lookup.py, safe-render.tsx, safe-pipeline.py (code); native/LegacyProfileView, native/MeasuredCardStack; plain-register, plain-register-clean (prose). Five design fixtures were also PROMOTED from coverage-boundary to positive in the same release -- uncommitted-radius, token-drift, missing-states, fixed-desktop-shell, vh-bottom-bar -- because 2.1.0 shipped a rule for the tell each of them had been recording as unreachable.

fixtures.note: Known false negative: useeffect-setstate matches per line, and this fixture's useEffect sets state a few lines down. Recorded honestly rather than relabelled -- the harness exists to surface rule-tuning candidates, not to hide them.

rounded-everything was REMOVED as a label in 1.7.0. The fixture holds exactly one radius hit, a rounded-full icon wrapper, and the tell is 'the same radius on every interactive control'. The floor rule clears a lone utility-class hit, so the old label could only have been reached by a reviewer breaking its own rule. The tell's real home is now uniform-control-radius.html. Found independently by ui-craft 0.2.4 in the copy of this same fixture.

The dimensionless was always planted here; it became reachable in 2.1.0, when .html joined the code surfaces. Before that, img-no-dimensions -- a CLS rule whose entire target syntax is -- could not fire on plain HTML at all.
Clean control: two small avatar pills and one line of real copy. rounded-full on an 8px avatar is a lone utility-class hit, which the floor rule clears.
Item 1 positive control. The only planted tell is the verbatim unmodified Tailwind hero run on the h1; every other decision on the page is committed. Paired with responsive-type-clean.html.

Item 1 clean control, and the guard against the regression this release exists to stop. Carries BOTH a fluid clamp() ramp AND a stepped Tailwind ramp on non-default steps with tuned tracking, plus the canonical prefers-reduced-motion block. A finding against any of them means the hero rule has been read as a ban on responsive type rather than on one copy-pasted string, and the 'fix' would break WCAG 1.4.4 and 2.3.3.

Concentration positive control for rounded-everything: five interactive controls all at rounded-full with no radius identity stated. This is what the tell actually describes, and it is what frosted-nav-neon.html never contained.

Exactly one presence-flaggable fingerprint (gradient text on a hero word) on an otherwise committed editorial page. The gradient is a warm terra-to-amber ramp, so the purple rules must NOT co-fire -- that is the half of presence-vs-concentration a positive-only fixture cannot test.

The tasteful-default combination in full: cream background + Instrument Serif display + sage accent, so all three legs fire the combination rule. generic-font also fires on the Inter button face; ui-craft accepts that as a permitted T1 fallback, anti-slop's rule does not distinguish fallback from primary, and the label records what this scanner actually reports.

Clean control with a committed point of view (tactical operator: warm-coal surface, single amber accent, square corners, fluid type). Mono appears only inside the log pane, which is genuine machine output; the readouts use tabular-nums on the system sans.

Clean control for the responsive doctrine. Uses every construct the catalogue prescribes -- clamp() ramps, width: min(), auto-fit minmax, container queries, 100dvh, safe-area insets, a visible focus ring -- and must produce ZERO findings.

Plants D1, an uncommitted 8px radius on every control, as three LITERAL border-radius declarations with no --radius token anywhere in the file. Promoted from coverage-boundary in 2.1.0: uniform-literal-radius reads exactly that shape, and is silenced on any file that states a radius identity. rounded-everything still does not see it -- that rule keys on rounded-2xl/3xl/full and 999px pills.

Plants hardcoded off-token colours and off-scale spacing that bypass the file's own token system. Promoted from coverage-boundary in 2.1.0 for the spacing half: three --space tokens declared and three off-4px-grid raw values (11px, 17px, 9px). The off-token COLOURS remain unruled and this fixture must not be cited as evidence that they are clean.

Plants a happy-path-only data UI and a non-functional Refresh control. Promoted from coverage-boundary in 2.1.0 for the dead control only: onclick="/* TODO: wire refresh */" is locally decidable from the line. The missing empty/error/loading states stay a permanent coverage boundary -- a single-file regex cannot distinguish a component with no empty state from one whose empty state lives in a sibling file.

Plants a fixed-pixel page shell that cannot resize: width: 1200px on the shell, width: 640px on the lede, grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 360px). Promoted from coverage-boundary in 2.1.0 -- the web analogue of the shipped native fixed-content-frame and fixed-grid-columns rules.
Plants a component laid out by a viewport media query where a container query belongs.

Plants a 100vh surface whose fixed bottom bar ignores dvh and the safe-area inset. Promoted from coverage-boundary in 2.1.0. The rule is file-scoped rather than line-scoped because the progressive-enhancement idiom writes its fallback on the next line; the missing env(safe-area-inset-bottom) on the bar itself stays unruled.

rounded-everything was REMOVED as a label in 1.7.0 for the same reason as frosted-nav-neon.html: two border-radius:999px declarations (.btn and .pill) is not maximal rounding on every control. uniform-literal-radius was ADDED in 2.1.0 and is a different claim about the same file: four literal border-radius values and no --radius token to vary from. Everything else on this fixture still fires.
Native positive control. Plants all five native tells: UIScreen.main.bounds, a fixed content frame, a device-idiom branch, a fixed GridItem array, and an ungated repeating symbol effect.

Native clean control: the same screen built by negotiation -- intrinsic sizing, a size-class branch, an adaptive grid, a measure cap rather than a leftover-sized value, ViewThatFits with an honest fallback, a one-shot haptic. The native counterpart of responsive-type-clean.html.

Authored in 2.1.0 to give the documented-fingerprint rules their first positives, and to close the two zero-fixture design rules the coverage sweep found. The gradient is from-indigo-500 to-violet-600 rather than to-blue: that is purple-gradient-default without also being purple-blue-gradient, so the two rules stay separable. ai-purple-class is labelled because the same two class tokens are its concentration threshold -- it is a genuine second finding on one composition, not a duplicate.

Three concentration rules at their thresholds and no further: two transition-all, three py-20/py-24 sections, two !important declarations. The !important pair sits outside any prefers-reduced-motion block, which is what the rule's suppress guard exists to protect -- see design/near-miss-controls.html for the guarded direction.

Both legs of missing-alt on one page: an img with no alt at all, and an img whose alt is the placeholder word 'photo'. outline: none is on :focus with no :focus-visible rule anywhere in the file, which is the only shape outline-none fires on. The first img carries width/height and the second does not, so img-no-dimensions fires once rather than twice.

The corpus had no raw-CSS fixture at all, although several design rules target raw CSS and .css is a web surface. Four geometry rules proven on a stylesheet rather than on markup with a style block. Paired with design/tokens-clean.css, which is the same file rewritten against a stated token system.

Raw-CSS clean control, and the correct-idiom twin of design/legacy-theme.css: width: min(), margin-inline, 100dvh, repeat(auto-fit, minmax()), var(--space-*) throughout, var(--radius), a :focus-visible ring, named transition properties, and a prefers-reduced-motion block. It must produce ZERO findings, which is what makes it a control rather than a file that happens to be quiet.

Exercises the suppressed-capture path on the design surface, which no corpus fixture reached before 2.1.0. The gradient-text composition is real and is opted out on the line with a stated reason, so the default two-argument scan is silent while scanContent(..., { collectSuppressed: true }) reports one suppressed design-tell. See test/scanner.test.mjs for the assertion in both directions.

Near-miss control for every rule added in 2.1.0: max-width: 1200px (the lookbehind), a width inside a one-line @media (the suppress), repeat(2, 1fr) and repeat(auto-fit, minmax()), text-xs uppercase tracking-tight, a blur-3xl with no rounded-full sibling, one transition-all, py-20 beside py-12 and py-32, a real currency figure, product-specific copy, a wired onclick, an img with real alt and dimensions, two literal radii, and outline: none silenced by a :focus-visible rule. Each construct sits one token away from a rule and none of them may fire.

The 2.1.0 JS/TS bug-class rules on one realistic component. .tsx is both a code surface and a web surface, so this fixture also proves the design table stays silent on a component that carries no design tell.

The Python-side security rules plus the three comment-slop rules. apologetic-comment and deferral-comment fire on different comments and never on the same one: the apologetic rule owns 'simplified implementation' and the deferral rule takes only the noun form, so the two cannot double-report. banner-comment counts four lines across two banners, which is its concentration threshold twice over. 2.1.1 adds the Python dead branch (if False:), the colon form the rule gained after shipping JS-only in 2.1.0.

A helper pasted in from an answer: an oaicite citation token in the header comment and an if (true) wrapper nobody removed. model-tooling-artifact is registered in both CODE_PATTERNS and TEXT_CONSTRUCTS; prose/plain-register.md is the other half of its coverage.

Exercises three families of the suppressed-capture path on the code surface in one file: a banned word in a hatched comment, a banned phrase in a hatched string literal, and a hatched innerHTML assignment. The default scan is silent; collectSuppressed reports three entries, all suppressedBy escape-hatch.

Plants SQL injection by f-string interpolation and by string concatenation. Both are real defects and this scanner has no rule for either: confidence-and-evidence.md lists the injection family as agent territory, because deciding whether a value is attacker-controlled needs the call graph. This file must never be cited as evidence that a scan cleared SQL injection.

Near-miss control for the JS/TS rules added in 2.1.0, using the counter-examples each rule was drafted against: DOMPurify.sanitize inside dangerouslySetInnerHTML, Promise.all over an async .map, catch (error: unknown), @ts-expect-error with a reason, a template literal holding complete class names, a lookup table, while (true), ready === true, a handler whose body has real work after its comment, a decorative alt="" with dimensions, a divider comment carrying content, and Buffer.from.

The Python half of the same near-miss set: an argument-list subprocess call, yaml.safe_load, yaml.load with an explicit SafeLoader, json.loads, datetime.now(timezone.utc), a comment referencing a tracked issue by number rather than deferring, and a 'Minimal repro' comment that is not an apology.

The two native rules added in 2.1.0. Three hardcoded .font(.system(size:)) calls with no relativeTo: and no @ScaledMetric, and exactly three DispatchQueue.main.async hops, which is where the concentration rule starts: one bridge from a legacy delegate callback is legitimate and stays below it.

Native coverage boundary. Nested GeometryReaders compute a split that a layout container would give for free, and feed sub-100pt fixed frames. GeometryReader overuse is a documented tell with no rule -- a proposed one was rejected because the legitimate uses outnumber the misuse -- and every frame here is below the >= 100pt threshold fixed-content-frame draws, so the file is honestly silent rather than clean.

The prose additions of 2.1.0. The antithesis is the 'not about X, it's about Y' reframe the qualifier set could not previously reach; the collocations are 'quietly building' and 'decisions compound', which is exactly the minCount of 2; the tooling token is a contentReference/oaicite pair. Paired with prose/plain-register-clean.md.

Near-miss control for the prose rules added or widened in 2.1.0: 'Interest compounds annually' (subject outside the collocation list), 'held the space open' (not the bare metaphor), 'The signal that the sensor emits' (not 'sends a signal that'), a single collocation (below minCount), 'It's not about money.' as one clause with no second clause to complete the antithesis, and a [1] footnote, a :::note admonition and an attributedString identifier, none of which is a model tooling token.
